definitions.explanation: A group of students who study together, or a lesson/course. From English 'class.'

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}のクラスは30{人|にん}です。
examples.english: There are 30 people in my class.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}のクラスは{楽|たの}しいです。
クラスメートと{仲|なか}がいいです。
examples.english: I get along well with my classmates.

notes:
LOANWORD:
クラス comes from English "class" and is commonly used in Japanese schools for homeroom classes.

RELATED TERMS:
- クラスメート: classmate
- {組|くみ}: class grouping (1{組|くみ}, 2{組|くみ}, etc.)
- {教室|きょうしつ}: classroom (the physical room)
- {学級|がっきゅう}: class (formal term)
- {授業|じゅぎょう}: lesson, class period

USAGE NOTE:
In Japanese schools, クラス refers to the homeroom group that stays together throughout the year, while {授業|じゅぎょう} refers to individual subject classes or lessons.

Also used in other contexts: ファーストクラス (first class), クラス{分|わ}け (class assignment).
